correctness.rationale: Every generic direction has exactly r negative normal scalar products in a consecutive block and illuminates exactly r-1 vertices; boundary directions illuminate at most r-2. Incidence counting yields the sharp integer and fractional inequalities \(I^{(k)}(P)\ge\lceil 2rk/(r-1)\rceil\) and \(I^*(P)\ge 2r/(r-1)\). Floor-distributed starts for \(N=\lceil 2rk/(r-1)\rceil\) have every cyclic interval of \(r-1\) labels occupied at least \(k\) times; equal cell weights attain fractional lower bound. Equality forces no boundary-cell mass and all cyclic coverage equalities, giving \(w_i=w_{i-(r-1)}\), with \(\gcd(2r,r-1)\) equal to one or two. Positive rational edge lengths close and successive cross-products are positive in the nonequiangular, noncentral hexagon example. Exact script 1950 finite combinatorial cases; universal validity is analytic.

Gorodzha 2026 abstract describes a global sharp upper bound and parallelotope equality, not this exact intermediate value or parity of optimizers, though full text was inaccessible. The identified published comparisons contained no dominating statement. Main originality contribution: the full optimal-face classification and the new non-equiangular noncentral class. value.rationale: Motivated by the explicitly posed determination of multiple illumination for convex polygons, the theorem solves all integer multiplicities for the substantial and naturally geometric class of antipodally paired edge-normal fans, which contains nonequiangular and noncentrosymmetric members. Beyond known numerical regular-polygon values it identifies all optimal fractional cell-weight vectors and a parity dichotomy (unique versus a one-dimensional simplex). These structural conclusions are not formal renamings of a regular case or generic universal bound; limitations to the stated normal fan and existing-source risk are explicit.
